data.title: B4U Booking Velocity Anomaly — Same Payment Method Booking Across Multiple OTAs/Hotels in Rapid Succession
data.description: Detects Buy-for-You (B4U) booking fraud patterns where the same payment method is used to make travel bookings across multiple OTAs, airlines, or hotel chains within a 24-hour period, especially when bookings are made for different travelers. B4U operators use stolen payment credentials to purchase travel at legitimate platforms, then resell bookings at 30-60% of face value. Sumsub estimates B4U services generate $37B in annual travel fraud losses. The velocity of bookings across disparate merchants with mismatched traveler names is the hallmark detection signal.

detection.condition: selection AND filter_velocity AND filter_multi_merchant AND filter_multi_traveler

enrichment_required.source: Rolling 24-hour count of bookings per payment method
Distinct merchant count per payment method in 24-hour window
Distinct traveler name count per payment method in 24-hour window

queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for B4U Booking Velocity Anomaly — DL-0181")`
`comment("Detects same payment method booking across multiple OTAs/hotels in rapid succession")`
index=flame_payments sourcetype=flame:travel_bookings
  (transaction_type="travel_booking" OR transaction_type="hotel_reservation"
   OR transaction_type="flight_purchase" OR transaction_type="car_rental")
| bin _time span=24h
| stats dc(merchant_name) as unique_merchants,
        dc(traveler_name) as unique_travelers,
        dc(destination_city) as unique_destinations,
        count as booking_count,
        sum(transaction_amount) as total_amount,
        values(traveler_name) as traveler_names,
        values(merchant_name) as merchants,
        values(destination_city) as destinations
  by payment_method_hash, _time
| where booking_count >= 3 AND unique_merchants >= 2
| eval risk_score = case(
    booking_count >= 6 AND unique_merchants >= 4 AND unique_travelers >= 3, "critical",
    booking_count >= 4 AND unique_merchants >= 3 AND unique_travelers >= 2, "high",
    1=1, "medium")
| eval traveler_count = mvcount(traveler_names)
| where traveler_count >= 2
| table payment_method_hash, _time, booking_count, unique_merchants,
        unique_travelers, unique_destinations, total_amount,
        traveler_names, merchants, destinations, risk_score
| sort - booking_count
queries.sql:
-- SQL for B4U Booking Velocity Anomaly
-- Detects same payment method used for multiple travel bookings with different travelers
SELECT
  b.payment_method_hash,
  CAST(b.booking_date AS DATE) AS booking_day,
  COUNT(*) AS booking_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT b.merchant_name) AS unique_merchants,
  COUNT(DISTINCT b.traveler_name) AS unique_travelers,
  COUNT(DISTINCT b.destination_city) AS unique_destinations,
  SUM(b.transaction_amount) AS total_amount,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT b.traveler_name, ', ') AS traveler_names,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT b.merchant_name, ', ') AS merchants,
  CASE
    WHEN COUNT(*) >= 6 AND COUNT(DISTINCT b.merchant_name) >= 4 THEN 'critical'
    WHEN COUNT(*) >= 4 AND COUNT(DISTINCT b.merchant_name) >= 3 THEN 'high'
    ELSE 'medium'
  END AS risk_score
FROM travel_bookings b
WHERE b.transaction_type IN ('travel_booking', 'hotel_reservation',
                              'flight_purchase', 'car_rental')
  AND b.booking_date >= DATEADD(HOUR, -24, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
GROUP BY b.payment_method_hash, CAST(b.booking_date AS DATE)
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
   AND COUNT(DISTINCT b.merchant_name) >= 2
   AND COUNT(DISTINCT b.traveler_name) >= 2
ORDER BY booking_count DESC
queries.cql:
// CrowdStrike CQL for B4U Booking Velocity Anomaly
(transaction_type="travel_booking" OR transaction_type="hotel_reservation"
 OR transaction_type="flight_purchase" OR transaction_type="car_rental")
| groupBy(payment_method_hash, function=[
    count(as=booking_count),
    countDistinct(merchant_name, as=unique_merchants),
    countDistinct(traveler_name, as=unique_travelers),
    countDistinct(destination_city, as=unique_destinations),
    sum(transaction_amount, as=total_amount),
    collect([traveler_name, merchant_name, destination_city])
  ], span=24h)
| booking_count >= 3
| unique_merchants >= 2
| unique_travelers >= 2
| sort(booking_count, order=desc)

references: Sumsub, Travel Fraud: The Hidden Epidemic (2026)
Riskified, OTA Fraud Patterns and Detection Strategies
falsepositives: Corporate travel managers booking for multiple employees using a company card
Travel agencies making legitimate bookings for multiple clients
Family vacation bookings across multiple platforms for price comparison
Event organizers booking group travel for conferences or weddings
